# Native Floating-Root Tangent Derivatives (Provisional)

## Physical and Numerical State

F05c (#11920, parent #11789) creates a small native MuJoCo 3.8 fixture with
one unactuated floating root, two connected hinges and two direct unit-gain
hinge motors. It deliberately has $n_q=9$, $n_v=8$, $n_u=2$; the free-root
unit quaternion contributes four configuration numbers but only three
angular tangent velocities. This prevents a Euclidean $q$/$v$ shortcut.
The admitted fixture is gravity-free and contact-free, with no plugin,
activation state, hidden assistance or external load. Both motors have
distinct names, ordered target joints and explicit torque limits. Native
Euler integration is fixed at 10 ms. RK4 is rejected at this derivative
boundary because the native transition-derivative API does not support it.

For the full native step $x^+=F_h(x,u)$, MuJoCo's
[`mjd_transitionFD`](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.8.0/computation.html#derivatives)
returns $A=\partial\delta x^+/\partial\delta x$ and
$B=\partial\delta x^+/\partial u$ on
$\delta x=(\delta q_{\mathrm{tan}},\delta v)\in\mathbb R^{16}$.
The code restores the complete `mjSTATE_INTEGRATION` state, computes the
native derivative, and independently steps a fresh state with the identical
held motor command. Tests perturb the quaternion and hinge coordinates using
`mj_integratePos`, then compare the next positions using
`mj_differentiatePos`, rather than subtracting quaternion components.
[MuJoCo's computation documentation](https://mujoco.readthedocs.io/en/3.8.0/computation.html)
describes this $n_q/n_v$ distinction and the discrete transition Jacobian.
Selected columns of $A$ and both ordered motor columns of $B$ match
independent centered native-step differences within $2\times10^{-4}$.

The two motor commands also undergo a separate full-state replay check:
three executed 10 ms ZOH torque rows plus an unused terminal sentinel are
bound through the pinned Tools T01 bundle with the exact source model,
native integration-state schema, time grid, actuator order and policy.
A fresh native model receives only the frozen time-indexed torques and
reproduces the complete integration-state trajectory within $10^{-12}$.
The fixture's unactuated root reacts through the plant dynamics; no root
force is injected or relabeled as a motor command. Actuator order reversal
reverses $B$ columns and the T01 channel order, while preserving the same
physical next state when commands are permuted accordingly. Out-of-limit
torques, commands at a limit where centered control derivatives are
nonsmooth, hidden gravity compensation and a mismatched integrator fail
admission. Compiled collision-enabled geometry fails admission even if the
initial state has no active contact.

## Timing and Qualification Boundary

The source-hashed development receipt
`docs/development/feedback_controls/F05C_NATIVE_TANGENT_RECEIPT_MJ38.json`
binds the supported provider, source files, Tools pin, model/input/initial
state/policy/time-grid digests and all four native tests. Ten repeated
derivative calls on the declared WSL host had median 1.56 ms, p95 3.23 ms
and worst 3.61 ms. The first Tools T01 bundle construction took 3.37 s
under cold import and independent replay took 0.060 s. These are observed
local timings; the 10 ms step does not become a hard control deadline from
the derivative-only figure. There is no source observation grid or measured
motion-capture error in this fixture.

This child establishes a multi-DOF manifold derivative and actual-input
replay boundary, **not** a multi-DOF optimized-controller win. The
linearized plant has not been promoted to contact-aware BoxFDDP, a full-body
model, muscle excitation control, grip/ground physics, six-engine parity or
private-capture matching. F02 TVLQR remains the broader fallback and F05
parent acceptance remains open. The canonical calculation inventory stays
blocked pending those qualification gates.
